title: A Senufo balafon amplifies its notes with gourds
body: The Senufo balafon from parts of West Africa is a tuned wooden percussion instrument. Calabash gourds of different sizes hang beneath its keys and resonate when a player strikes the wood.
takeaway: The material under an instrument can shape a note as much as the piece the musician hits.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Senufo Balafon, Decision 6.COM 13.29 (2011)
visual: a wooden balafon seen close up with hanging gourd resonators

title: Traditional Japanese washi can be made from mulberry bark
body: To make traditional washi, craft workers use fibres from the paper mulberry plant. They spread the fibres in water and lift them on a screen, letting the water drain so a new sheet forms.
takeaway: A sheet of paper begins as interlaced fibres held together as they dry, rather than as a solid layer poured into shape.
visual: a papermaker lifting a wet sheet on a screen above a wooden vat
